clue.text: Big payouts make bundled notes for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of words, signals the swap here
for here means as said by, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to pack things is to make them into a bundle
jots are brief written notes

explanation.surface: Someone advises tying banknotes into wads before handing over large sums.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the bundle word is PAK; 'for Spooner' swaps its opening sound with that of the notes word, and the phrase is heard as JACK POTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackpots are the largest prizes in a lottery or on a gaming machine, so they are huge winnings.

clue.text: Record cuts in joke coat

indicators.note: something that cuts in breaks into the other word, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to josh is to joke or tease
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record interrupts a comedy routine about an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts in' puts the record inside the joke word. 'joke coat' looks like a phrase for a novelty garment, but 'coat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joseph is a long caped riding coat once worn by women, named after Joseph's garment in Genesis.

clue.text: See 20
Thermoplastic stuff needed by girl to keep law

indicators.note: the outer letters keep, or hold, the law word inside them
the stuff word is needed by, so placed before, the girl word

parts.note: to pig is to stuff oneself greedily
a lass is a girl
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A girl needs plastic material in order to comply with the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like part of the definition, but it is the verb meaning to eat greedily; 'needed by' puts it before the girl, and 'to keep' has the pair hold the Latin for law.
explanation.definitionFit: Plexiglas is a trade name for acrylic sheeting, a plastic that softens when heated and can be remoulded.

clue.text: Factor this colour represents in Beaufort scale?

indicators.note: read as re-presents: the letters are presented again in a new order

parts.note: the letters of this phrase make the anagram pool
the letters of this word are taken out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A question about which colour stands for a given force on the scale of wind speeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Take F, A, C, T, O, R out of BEAUFORT SCALE and B, E, U, S, A, L, E are left; 'represents' rearranges them. The Beaufort scale measures wind force by the state of the sea, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea blue is a shade of blue like the colour of the open ocean.

clue.text: It's circulated in good company for supping a little vino after meal finally over

definitions.text: It's circulated in good company for supping a little vino after meal finally over

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word meal

parts.note: the word meal supplies its last letter

indicators.note: the circulated letters sup, or take in, the bit of vino
circulated sends a letter round from the back of the group to its front
a little of vino is just its first letter

parts.note: the word vino supplies its first letter
up means over, as in time is up

explanation.surface: At a formal dinner, once the meal is finished, a cup of wine is passed round the friendly gathering for each to sip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal finally' starts it. 'circulated' moves the last letter of the group to the front, giving OINGC, which is 'supping' the V that is 'a little' of vino, making OVINGC. The blogger read 'circulated' as reversing company alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A loving cup is a large shared drinking vessel passed round the table at banquets so each guest drinks from it.

clue.text: Fine wines taken out of case

indicators.note: taking the word out of its case strips its outer letters, leaving the middle

parts.note: Tokays are sweet Hungarian wines

explanation.surface: Bottles have been unpacked from their crate without trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out of case' removes T and S, the casing letters of TOKAYS; 'case' looks like a case of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is an informal synonym for satisfactory or all right, as in 'I'm fine'.

clue.text: 28 Across new client's accepted rent going up

indicators.note: the rearranged letters accept, or take in, the reversed word
new signals that the letters of client are made into a new arrangement
in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A new client has agreed to a rise in rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLIENT to INLECT, which has 'accepted' TEL, LET 'going up'. 28 Across is THINKING, the noun for mental power.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning, the same thing as one's thinking or mental power.

clue.text: Energise doctor, holding in urge to dance

indicators.note: the doctor letters hold the rest inside them

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: letters made to dance are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor suppresses the desire to dance in order to perk himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the verb to tamper with; here it is GP, 'holding' IN plus GERU, URGE made 'to dance'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ginger up is a British idiom for making something livelier, the way ginger adds zest.

clue.text: See 19
Cocktail counter attached to top function

parts.note: a man is a playing piece or counter in draughts or chess
a top hat, or just a hat, covers the top of the head
tan is short for tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A bar counter linked to some higher-level operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a bar counter; it is a game piece. Tan is the trigonometric tangent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a mixed drink of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters.

clue.text: In Monk's Head Tavern, drunk "helps" young woman downstairs

indicators.note: the head of the word Monk's is its opening letter

parts.note: the word Monk's supplies its first letter
aids means helps

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters of tavern are tipsily jumbled

explanation.surface: In a pub named the Monk's Head, a drunk patron gets a waitress to help out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk's Head Tavern' reads as a pub name; 'drunk' makes TAVERN into ERVANT. 'downstairs' points to the servants' quarters of a big house.
explanation.definitionFit: A maidservant is a female domestic servant, who worked below stairs in a large household.

clue.text: Who's 2 Down given 2 Down Christmas items?

parts.note: 2 Down is CRAZY, and someone who is crazy is a nut
crackers is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A question asking who is daft enough to be handed daft festive things.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces mean crazy (2 Down): a nut is a crazy person and crackers is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcrackers are a tool for cracking nuts, set out at Christmas when bowls of nuts are traditional.

clue.text: Curry is this spicy, doing for current CERN staff?

indicators.note: to curry is to cook in spices, so the letters are worked over into a new order
doing for means getting rid of, so this letter is removed

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A question about whether a curry is this hot, as tasted by the staff at the research centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like the dish but is the anagram signal; 'doing for' removes one I (current) from IS THIS SPICY before the rest is rearranged. CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva.
explanation.definitionFit: CERN is a particle physics laboratory, so its scientists are experts in physics.

clue.text: See 4
Clown and mechanic supported by different factions?

parts.note: Bip was the white-faced clown character played by the mime Marcel Marceau
an old sense of mechanic is a manual worker or artisan

explanation.surface: A clown and a mechanic each have backing from different groups.
explanation.walkthrough: Bip is Marcel Marceau's mime clown. Mechanic is used in its old sense of a skilled manual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipartisan policy is backed by two parties at once, with both sides of politics in agreement.

clue.text: Worried less — if ever — about constant DIY

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the constant
worried means pulled about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: C is a common symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics

explanation.surface: Someone frets less than ever about constantly having to do jobs themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' rearranges LESS IF EVER to SELFSERVIE, which goes 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-it-yourself means doing a task without help from staff, as when customers serve themselves.

clue.text: Piecemeal introduces standard measure in small quantities

indicators.note: one word introduces the other into itself, taking it inside

parts.note: singly means one at a time, piece by piece
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: A step-by-step approach brings in a standard unit of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piecemeal' looks like the definition, but it is the word that 'introduces' the standard measure into itself after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something sparingly is to use it frugally, a little at a time.

clue.text: See 28
Roo possibly went against the grain

parts.note: a cross is a rood, and with its end cut off a rood becomes the word Roo

explanation.surface: Perhaps the kangaroo behaved contrarily.
explanation.walkthrough: Roo wants to be the kangaroo from Winnie-the-Pooh, but it is ROOD, a church cross, with its last letter cut: a cross cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To crosscut is to saw wood across its fibres rather than along them.

clue.text: See 5
It's not natural rating restaurant trolley's wheels

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
a cart is a trolley, and the apostrophe S adds an S

explanation.surface: A low score for a restaurant's dessert trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' reads like the trolley's castors, but it turns the restaurant-and-trolley pair round to STRACTART. A rating is a sailor below officer rank; a trattoria is an Italian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract art does not depict nature or things realistically, so it is non-representational.

clue.text: In charges libertine, wanting my pity

indicators.note: a libertine is free of restraint, so the letters are let loose into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A debauched man in charge of others shows no compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'libertine' is an unusual anagram signal, read as free and loose; IN CHARGES is 'wanting' MY to complete the letters that are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A crying shame is a great pity, something regrettable that should not have happened.

clue.text: Prison film reviews retracted line about walls of Alcatraz

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: crits is informal for critiques or reviews

indicators.note: the line letters go about, or around, the other pair

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a line

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the walls of Alcatraz are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Critics took back their verdict on a movie about the famous island jail.
explanation.walkthrough: CRITS 'retracted' gives STIRC; the 'walls of Alcatraz' are AZ, and RY goes 'about' them to make RAZY. Stir is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir Crazy is a 1980 comedy starring Gene Wilder and Richard Pryor as men wrongly jailed.

clue.text: A caging area for each game not the threat it seems

indicators.note: the outer word cages, or encloses, the other pieces

parts.note: a can mean per, as in five pounds a head
per means for each
tig is the playground chasing game also called tag

explanation.surface: A cage for animals in a game park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not the letter but the word per, as in 'twice a day'; it is 'caging' A, PER and TIG. Tig is a British name for tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger is a person or power that appears dangerous but is in fact weak.

clue.text: In the beginning God created … great talents

parts.note: these words open Genesis, the book abbreviated Gen
these words come in chapter i, verse i, of Genesis

explanation.surface: Quoting the Bible's opening line, then trailing off to praise outstanding gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Genesis 1:1, written Gen. i. i in the old style with Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genius, here meaning people of exceptional ability.

clue.text: See 27
Is 28 Across about answer — get so agitated over it

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit over, or cover, the word it
agitated means shaken up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mulling over an answer gets worked up about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges the letters into OGATES, which goes 'over' the word it to make OGITATES. 28 Across is THINKING, so the definition is 'is thinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder something.

clue.text: Indulge in repasts, periodically

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, here every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of repasts

explanation.surface: Someone allows themselves a proper meal from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes every other letter of rEpAsTs, and the result is also what you do at repasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, which is what one does at meals.

clue.text: Saffie's first home on Classic mount

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Saffie's

parts.note: the word Saffie's supplies its opening letter
in means at home
A1 means first-class or classic, written AI

explanation.surface: Saffie first lived on a famous mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes S from Saffie's. AI stands for A1, top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the mountain where, in the Bible, Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Will outfitter's assistant recommend this audacious behaviour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shop assistant suggests putting a garment on to see if it fits
second meaning: chancing your luck to see what you can get away with

explanation.walkthrough: Trying it on is the British idiom for cheekily testing how far you can go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both testing clothes for fit in a shop and cheekily pushing your luck.

clue.text: Limit for Henry VIII, not(!) what to wear when working out

definitions.text: what to wear when working out

parts.note: Henry VIII was famously stout, so he was not a thin king
a cap is a limit, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: A cap on something for Henry VIII, then a quip about gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(!)' flags the joke: Henry VIII was not a THIN KING. 'working out' is solving a problem, not exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on one's thinking cap is the idiom for concentrating on solving a problem.
